items.title: Blink-182 and Pierce the Veil to Headline When We Were Young 2027
items.summary:
When We Were Young will return to the Las Vegas Festival Grounds on October 16, 2027, with Blink-182 and Pierce the Veil at the top of the bill. The 7-Eleven-presented festival is coming back after skipping 2026 entirely, making this its fifth edition.

Variety reported the lineup, which runs deep into the emo, pop-punk and alt-rock catalog: Limp Bizkit, Third Eye Blind, The Used, All Time Low, Simple Plan, 5 Seconds of Summer, Circa Survive, Taking Back Sunday, Sleeping With Sirens, The Psychedelic Furs, Hot Mulligan, New Found Glory, Movements, Senses Fail, Neon Trees, Cartel, Plain White T's and Thursday, among others.

Organizers set a presale for November 20 at 10 a.m. PT, with the cheapest general admission tickets available during that first hour. Whatever is left goes to a general onsale an hour later at 11 a.m. PT.

The return follows an announcement this past February that the festival would sit out a year. Organizers did not give a specific reason, saying only: "After an unforgettable run in Las Vegas, we've decided to take 2026 off to give this festival the care it deserves and to make sure what comes next feels just as special as what came before." The statement added, "This isn't goodbye — it's just a pause."

When We Were Young began at the Observatory in Santa Ana, California, before moving to Las Vegas in 2022 and running there annually through 2025. Past headliners include Blink-182, Panic! at the Disco, My Chemical Romance and Paramore, which makes the 2027 bill a second turn at the top for Blink-182.

items.title: Jason Isbell & Drive-By Truckers Announce Summer Of Joy Tour
items.summary:
Jason Isbell and the 400 Unit will co-headline a North American tour with Drive-By Truckers next year, billed as the Summer of Joy. The run opens with two nights in Nashville at The Pinnacle on May 6 and 7, 2027, and closes September 7 at Cain's Ballroom in Tulsa.

The pairing carries some history. Isbell played in Drive-By Truckers from 2001 to 2007 before leaving to build a solo career in roots rock, and he has reunited with the band occasionally since — most recently last month at his ShoalsFest in Alabama, where the group performed its 2003 album Decoration Day in full.

Stereogum reported that a dollar from every ticket sold on the tour will go to Nuçi's Space, the Athens, Georgia nonprofit that works to prevent suicide by providing mental health resources along with rehearsal and performance space for local musicians.

The itinerary splits into clusters rather than one continuous stretch. A May leg runs through Tuscaloosa, New Orleans, St. Louis, La Vista, Denver, Red Rocks and Kansas City. The tour picks back up in late July with two nights at Atlanta's Fox Theatre, then moves through Richmond, Charlotte, Wolf Trap, Boston, Forest Hills Stadium, New Haven and Portland, Maine.

August brings Niagara Falls, Detroit's Fox Theatre, two nights at Chicago's Salt Shed, Indianapolis, Cincinnati, Asheville, two nights at DPAC in Durham, St. Augustine, Austin and Fort Worth, followed by a West Coast swing through the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles, the Santa Barbara Bowl, Berkeley's Greek Theatre and Lake Tahoe. September dates in Seattle, Portland, Park City and Dillon lead into the Tulsa finale.

Presale access begins the morning after the announcement, with general tickets going on sale Friday, November 20 at 10 a.m.

items.title: Jhené Aiko Announces 2027 Tour with H.E.R. and Swae Lee
items.summary:
Jhené Aiko has booked a 37-date North American tour for 2027, titled Ark to Agartha: A Westside Whimsy Experience. H.E.R., Swae Lee and Karri will join her across the run, which opens March 10 at Enterprise Center in St. Louis and ends May 21 at Crypto.com Arena in her hometown of Los Angeles.

The support lineup shifts partway through. Swae Lee and Karri handle opening duties for the first 10 shows, and H.E.R. joins beginning with the March 26 date at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, staying on through the rest of the tour.

The arena run supports Westside Whimsy, Aiko's fourth album, which arrived September 11 and marked her first new full-length in six years. Routing includes Minneapolis, Milwaukee, Kansas City, Columbus, Buffalo, Chicago, Detroit, Toronto, Boston, Washington D.C., Atlanta, Orlando, Memphis, New Orleans, Austin, Houston, Denver, Phoenix, Las Vegas, San Francisco, Portland, Seattle, Vancouver and Salt Lake City.

According to Consequence, tickets go through a staggered presale schedule before reaching the public. A Verizon Shine presale starts Wednesday, November 18 at 10 a.m. local time, followed by an artist presale at 2 p.m. that day for fans who sign up through Aiko's website. A Live Nation presale runs Thursday, November 19 at 10 a.m. local time for All Access members.

General onsale begins Friday, November 20 at 10 a.m. local time via Ticketmaster.
